extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of natural philosophy, mathematicians, and philosophical/theological skeptics
extracted.subtask_description: An expository philosophical argument that uses empirical laws of mechanics (gravity, motion, force composition) and mathematical observations (orbits, curves) to infer a first cause / divine agency and its attributes. Targeted at skeptics, mathematicians, and readers of natural theology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Attraction or Repulsion
rubrics_metrics.description: It is said, that the Body A ... has an Attractive or a Repulsive Force (Attracticem vel Repellencem) or otherwise, that the Body B gravitates to the Body A, when we see that another Body B is moved towards, or driven from A, without the Intervention of any other Bodies, which by protruding the said B, may be affirmed to produce such Motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for attributing attraction/repulsion: observe motion of a body toward or away from another in the absence of intervening bodies. Use experiments to distinguish direct attraction/repulsion from motion due to percussion/protrusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of Forces on Experimental Grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoſe therefore who make other Scruples and Difficulties, may conſult the famous Writings ... and allow of so many of the Arguments which are there uſed to demonſtrate this AttrafFion and Repulfion, as they think they fully proved the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the internal 'manner' of a force is not comprehensible, accept its operation when supported by repeated experiments and demonstrations (e.g., Newton, Huygens). Empirical demonstration can override speculative doubt about mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality of Gravity as Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: One of those Appearances of Nature which are so familiar to us ... the Gravity of all Bodies ... has oft occur'd to me as an irrefragable Proof of a Weak, Powerful and Gracious God ... that every thing which we call a Body ... falls, or is driven down with a certain Force, and by the shortest Way towards the Center of the Earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ubiquity, regularity and usefulness (e.g., seas remaining on bottoms, rains and rivers, support of life) of gravity as grounds for inferring design or a directing cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of Natural Laws to Heavenly Bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is astonishing, what modern Observations have render'd very probable, namely, That this Natural Law of Gravity extends itself thro' the whole visible Universe, and seems to prevail over all, even over the great Heavenly Bodies, which gravitate towards each other in the same Manner as the sublunary Bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: consistency of the same law (gravity) across scales (terrestrial and celestial) strengthens inference that the law is real and universal; observed planetary motions that match this law (elliptical orbits) are evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical confirmation via planetary perturbations
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Huygens demonstrates ... that Saturn ... and Jupiter ... when near each other ... Saturn, by reason of the Greatness of its actual Body and its Nearness to Jupiter ... must occasion some remarkable visible Effect: in the Satellites of Jupiter; ... the Satellites of Jupiter do change their usual Course ... agreeable to the said Law of Attraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use observed perturbations and mutual influences between bodies (e.g., planet-satellite interactions) as direct empirical evidence supporting attraction/gravity laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bodies move in straight lines unless acted on (Inertia Axiom)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is by Experience, that all Bodies being once put into Motion, pursue their Way in one and the same Right Line, if they do not meet with any Obstruction, nor are turn'd out of their Way by another Power; ... A Body being once at Rest, or in Motion, ceases not from that Rest, or from being moved in a Right Line ... unless another Force acting upon it produces a Change therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the inertia axiom as a foundational mechanical law (accepted by mathematicians) and use it as a premise in physical and philosophical arguments; it is supported by many mechanical experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportionality of motion to impressed forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The Motions, and all their Differences and Changes in all Bodies are greater and smaller in Proportion, as the Powers which impress the same upon those Bodies are greater or smaller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportionality (e.g., double the force -> double the motion) as a quantitative criterion linking causes (forces) to effects (motions); appeal to mechanicians (Wallis, Huygens) and experiments to justify proportional relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelogram (vector) composition of forces
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a Law in Nature, that in case two Powers do equally act upon a Body A ... the Body will be moved according to different Lines ... which are found and determined by drawing a Diagonal Line in the Parallelogram ... of which the Sides consist of the Lines along which the Body would be moved by each particular Power in the same time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use geometric construction (parallelogram of forces) to determine resultant direction and magnitude of combined forces; practical application: explaining projectile trajectories and many mechanical phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictability of projectile motion from combined forces
rubrics_metrics.description: It is known, that the Flight-Line of a Bullet discharged from a Cannon ... is determined merely by this Law of Nature; for as there are ... one, which ... impels it from A to K; and another, that of Gravity, which causes it to descend continually by the Lines AB, DL, EM, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply composition-of-forces and gravity laws to practical ballistics (gunnery and bombardry) to predict and control trajectories; experimental and mathematical knowledge converts seemingly uncontrollable motions into tractable problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of mathematical curves produced by gravity (catenary, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: We could here produce numberless Cases in which it may be proved, that ... thousands of Millions of others, and of the smallest Bodies, do describe Geometrical Curve-Lines, wherein the Law of the Line, according to all the Laws of Mathematicks, is preserved at all its Points. Thus ... the Catenaria or Chain-Line ... is produced by the Gravity ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use occurrence of precise mathematical forms in nature (catenary, projectile parabolas, elliptic orbits) as evidence that natural phenomena obey stable, discoverable laws—supporting inference to intelligent order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation and communication of motion implies a first cause
rubrics_metrics.description: The First Motion proves a God; as does also the Continuation and Communication of Motion. ... Motion does not belong to the Being of a Body. ... from all this it is easy to conclude, that no such Thing as a Body can be the first Cause of those Motions ... the first Cause thereof must be Incorporeal ... and infinitely Powerful, Wise, and Good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical criterion: because bodies are passive and motion must be imparted/continued, the origin and sustaining of motion point to an incorporeal first cause; use mathematical and experiential premises (inertia, proportionality, persistence) to argue to deity and to infer attributes (power, wisdom, goodness) from order and purposive effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mathematical demonstration and experiment as authoritative
rubrics_metrics.description: From which Principles, Sir Isaac Newton has shewn briefly in his Princip. Philo. ... that all the Laws of Motion, and the Rules of Mechanics do necessarily flow, and have given Instances thereof in all the Mechanical Powers. ... a great Number of Experiments have been made in Machines to confirm the same, by which this Law is with sufficient Certainty proved a Posteriori.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for accepting claims: combination of mathematical deduction and a posteriori experimental confirmation (appeal to Newton, Huygens, Mariotte, Wallis) provides strong warrant for the physical premises used in theological argumentation.
